chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Aunt Mae and Jess Jackson
summary: Aunt Mae's family and when she ran into Jess in 1955.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Okay, the next thing is going back on your father's side, one of the sisters was named Marietta, Aunt Mae, as you refer to her.
And I think you said her husband's name was Jess?
Yes, her husband's name was Jess Jones.
Jess Jones, okay. So he wasn't any relation to the cousin you have who also is named
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, Jess Jackson was Aunt Mae's sister's son. So Aunt Mae would be his aunt, and Jess would be his step-uncle.
Right. Okay, which of the sisters was his mother?
Alright, and you also said you had seen Jess a long time ago. Do you have any approximate recollection of when that was?

Yeah, I recall having run into Jess, it must have been around 1955. I was working in Detroit at a Club and he came by the hotel where I was stopping and we had a little conversation. He wasn't performing at that time. He had been a tap dancer working around Detroit. And when he was young he danced around Pittsburgh too. At the time when I talked with him he seemed to have been out of the business.
